newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen steady to lower, Dow to retest 6000.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen steady to lower, Dow to retest 6000.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to duplicate their performance of a day ago, when the Dow industrials overcame mild selling pressure to top 6000 on an intraday basis but failed to close above the milestone.
"I'm looking for the same trading pattern as yesterday, a little lower at the open and then a reversal," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
On Monday, despite clearing 6000 twice, the Dow eventually ran out of steam and closed lower as investors took profits from stocks' recent sharp rally.
In contrast, the Nasdaq Composite achieved its first record close since the massive sell-off in July.
"That was encouraging because it showed the broader market springing to life," Cardillo said.
Analysts said technology stocks were likely to pause for the session, ahead of this afternoon's release of monthly semiconductor book-to-bill data.
Economic data slated for release today include the BTM/Schroders and Redbook weekly retail sales reports and the September Richmond Fed survey.
The retail sales reports are not expected to show a marked departure from recent softness nor is the Richmond Fed survey considered a major factor today.

Late Monday, release of monthly consumer credit figures showed a dramatic slowdown in consumer borrowing growth. While the figure suggested a further slowing of the consumer side of the economy, analysts said other forces are also at play.
"Banks are finally cutting back on the amount of credit they're willing to give out," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities.
In Tokyo, stocks were lower as markets remained sluggish ahead of general elections on October 20. The Nikkei 225 index fell 122 points to close at 21,039.
In London, U.S. stocks were generally weaker in anticipation of further profit-taking in the U.S. The FTSE-100 fell five points to 4026.
The dollar was steady in Tokyo and in Europe, holding near 111 yen and 1.525 marks.
Bonds were little changed. The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury rose 1/32 to yield 6.79 percent.
The December S&P 500 index future fell 0.8 to 707.4.
The New York Times Marketplace Column reports that slumping share prices have diminished the value of several mergers in the communications industry.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column reports that shares in several securities firms, most recently PaineWebber Group, have risen on takeover speculation. Smaller regional firms are viewed as the most likely candidiates, the column said.
